As a suite grows, a serial run gets slow — each test waits for the one before it.
**Pabot** runs suites (or even individual tests) **in parallel**, each in its own
process, so a run that took a minute serially can finish in seconds.

Pabot is a drop-in: it produces the same `output.xml` as `robot`, so all your
reports, `rebot`, and CI wiring keep working unchanged.

```diagram
hub "Pabot splits a run across workers"
pabot #gear -- one command, many processes
alpha worker -- runs checks/alpha.robot
beta worker -- runs checks/beta.robot
merged output.xml #doc -- one file, every test
note "Same output.xml as robot, so rebot and reports still work"
```

## Task 1 — Run the suites in parallel

Run the two clean suites at the same time:

```bash
uv run pabot --outputdir results checks/alpha.robot checks/beta.robot
```

Both suites start at once and finish together:

```terminal
$ uv run pabot --outputdir results checks/alpha.robot checks/beta.robot
[0] EXECUTING Alpha
[1] EXECUTING Beta
[1] PASSED Beta in 0.5 seconds
[0] PASSED Alpha in 0.5 seconds
4 tests, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
```

Pabot runs `alpha` and `beta` concurrently and merges their results into one
`results/output.xml` — covering every test from both suites.

**Check:** the parallel run produces a report with all four tests, passing.
